correctness.rationale: For every positive (a,b,c,d), direct analysis of the two-run factor rectangles, forced full internal exponents for three- and four-run factors, and the iff criterion that the word is absent while both one-letter deletions occur produces a disjoint exhaustive eleven-row MAW list. Counting rows yields b+c+(1+[a>c])(1+[d>b]); geometric summation of four strict-comparison cases gives the rational bivariate series; elementary extremal inequalities yield max n-1 except n=6 (max n). The independently coded finite factor enumeration agrees with the entire list for 4096 quadruples, with direct maximal counts at n=4..21 and bivariate multiplicities through n=17. These checks are supplementary and do not substitute for the infinite proof. Boundary cases a=b=c=d=1, empty j ranges, equality a=c or d=b and the unique anomalous (2,1,1,2) are explicitly handled.

value.rationale: The first binary RLE class featuring two 01-occurrence rectangles and a competing splice of left/right extensions is exactly four runs. The complete forbidden-factor list, multiplicative 1/2/4 boundary correction, rational full length/count distribution and exceptional sharp n=6 extremum are structural, not a restatement of a generic enumeration algorithm. This is a naturally complete classification relevant to compressed-string antidictionaries and MAW enumeration rather than an arbitrary selected parameter value. It makes no claim of paper-scale or downstream algorithmic improvement.
